correctness.rationale: From the pinned centered least-squares normal equations, the even quadratic kernel is w_j=3(3m²+3m−1−5j²)/((2m+1)(4m²+4m−3)); its constant and quadratic moments are respectively one and zero. Cyclic forward differences range over precisely the zero-sum subspace; pairing positive and negative masses into e_i−e_j proves its convolution ℓ1 norm is (1/2)max_{s≠0}Σ_i|c_i−c_{i−s}|, attained by integrating e_0−e_s to a binary arc. Equality with Σ|c| is coordinatewise equivalent to no positive-positive or negative-negative overlap. Positives form length P=2a+1 arc and negative-shift distances are [1,m−b]∪[2b,2m]. Since P>m−b, both shift distances must lie in [P,2b−1]∪[2m+1,∞); integer sums yield exactly the claimed finite resonance and eventual half-line. Zero coefficients give b=a+2 rather than a+1. Verified independently exact rational radius-two values 1,47/35,44/35,47/35 and representative sign-support shifts at radii 2,3,6,10; these checks do not replace the all-m interval-sum argument. The m→∞ thresholds follow by floor asymptotics and a Riemann sum.

value.rationale: Sharp dimension-selective robustness is an independently motivated exact operator norm question for a standard smoothing filter. The isolated saturation, strict intermediate loss and permanent recovery are counterintuitive and specify precise cycle lengths needed by numerical analysts. The signed-support arithmetic is neither a renamed coefficient table nor a routine consequence of negative mass.

final_claim: For every integer quadratic Savitzky–Golay radius m>=2 and cyclic length n>=2m+1, the sharp adjacent-total-variation gain is half the maximum cyclic shift difference of the signed kernel; it equals full kernel absolute mass precisely for 2P_m<=n<=4b_m-2 or n>=P_m+2m+1, including zero-weight arithmetic exceptions. The five-tap gains at n=5,6,7,>=8 are 1,47/35,44/35,47/35.
limitations: Only real periodic equally spaced quadratic/cubic center smoothing with nonaliasing windows; no higher-order or irregular filters.
